name: Jehai
confidence_why: 4 independent first-hand sources agree (3 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification

audit.deciding_source_kind: database or survey citing another work
audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-dominant, final (final stress)' is correct and now verified against the primary reference grammar: Burenhult 2005 sec. 2.5.1 p.38 states non-contrastive stress invariably on the last syllable of the word, no secondary stress, applying equally to Malay loans (sec. 2.6.4 p.43 gives /ga'jah/ < Malay 'gajah as relocation to final); Burenhult 2001 MKS 31 p.43 is identical; Wikipedia's sentence is a faithful paraphrase. The record as filed rests on Wikipedia with grade carried-secondary only because the second reader could not reach the primary; the primary is now obtained (sealang PL-566 PDF with text layer). Action: replace the deciding citation with Burenhult 2005:38 sec. 2.5.1 (quote above), raise grade to typeset-pdf/primary, and optionally fill domain = word (final syllable of the word; Jahai affixation is prefixal/infixal so base-final = word-final; unstressed subject pronouns/c

sources.citation: Wikipedia, Jahai language, Stress and tone section (citing Burenhult 2005 A Grammar of Jahai); corroborates the first reading Burenhult p.38 quote (invariable final stress, no secondary stress, applies to loans).
sources.quote: The position of stress always falls on the last syllable.

sources.citation: Burenhult, Niclas. 2005. A Grammar of Jahai. Pacific Linguistics 566. Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, ANU. xiv+245 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'As also noted by Schebesta (1928a:805), Jahai has non-contrastive stress that falls invariably on the last syllable of a word, and there is no secondary stress. This applies as much to recent loans from Malay as to indigenous words.' Elsewhere: unstressed preverbal pronouns/clitics 'cannot receive stress'; reduplicant copies do not receive stress.
sources.locator: sec. 2.5.1 'Stress', p.38 (PDF p.52); also sec. 2.4.2 (final syllable 'always bears stress') and sec. 2.6.4 p.43 'Relocation of stress' (Malay loans get final stress: /ga'jah/ < 'gajah)
